A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NTK-DFL work, with matching core algorithms and experiments. Text, equations, figures, tables, and all appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on Fashion-MNIST, MNIST, and FEMNIST, including convergence comparisons, topology studies, and averaging ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, compression and communication measurements, and a reconstruction attack experiment.

M1.justification: Equation 1 and Algorithm 2 change uniform neighbor averaging to sample-count-weighted averaging. Appendix E adds data subsampling, sparsification, quantization, input projection, and clustered computation strategies. These extend the procedure substantially; Jacobian batching itself was already proposed in v1.

E1.justification: The three classification datasets and their tasks remain unchanged. v2 adds clustered and line network scenarios to the topology comparison and a limited image-reconstruction attack task in Appendix F.

E2.justification: DFedSAM becomes an evaluated comparator in Figures 2–3 and the new communication-volume comparison. v1 cited its underlying work but did not evaluate it. The existing DFL comparators and centralized NTK-FL comparison remain.

E3.justification: New experiments vary batching, subsampling, compression, and projection settings and evaluate accuracy against transmitted megabytes using compressed baselines. The original classification setup is largely retained. Appendix C.2 changes hyperparameter selection from 'best test' to 'best validation' accuracy but immediately retains the test-based selection description, leaving that particular revision ambiguous.

E4.justification: Appendices E–F add substantial analyses of batching, subsampling, successive compression techniques, communication-volume trade-offs, and reconstruction under compression. The topology analysis gains clustered and line graphs. Existing averaging, initialization, sparsity, and heterogeneity analyses remain, including material relocated to Appendix C.

E5.justification: The 95% confidence interval for random client-averaging order is retained from v1 Figure 5 in v2 Figure 6. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or introduces additional uncertainty-estimation procedures. The shared projection seed concerns implementation rather than statistical replication.

E6.justification: Figure 2 retains NTK-DFL's 12, 17, and 18 rounds for IID, alpha=0.5, and alpha=0.1, while adding DFedSAM entries of 24, 45, and 200+. New results cover additional topologies, batching and subsampling trends, compression-volume trade-offs, and impaired reconstruction with projection. These are added findings, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: v1 has algorithm equations but no convergence theorem. v2 adds Section 4 and Appendix G with formal objectives, mixing assumptions, NTK approximation-error bounds, Theorem 4.5, Corollary 4.6, and supporting proofs. It also corrects the exponential signs in Equation 4 and expands the mathematical description of weight evolution.

C1.justification: v2 retains the first-NTK-DFL and 4.6-times-fewer-rounds claims, but removes the headline claim of at least 10% improvement over mean client accuracy. Its contributions now include compression robustness and theoretically improved convergence rates. The conclusion also removes the earlier characterization of the method as privacy-preserving.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes fewer communication rounds from lower communication volume and explains when the former is advantageous. It adds interpretations of batching, compression, reconstruction vulnerability, and the trade-off between local iterations and NTK approximation error. Appendix C.1 also acknowledges that the busiest-node matching protocol disadvantages centralized NTK-FL.

D1.justification: v2 adds a source-code access link, differential-equation-solver implementation details, DFedSAM hyperparameters, and disclosure of one gossip step per round. Appendices E–F specify compression, sampling, projection, and attack settings. These materially expand reproducibility information without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v2 adds references concerning sparsification, SAM, DFL surveys, modern-architecture NTKs, and medical federated learning, and compares its convergence bound with Sun et al. The main research positioning remains intact. Sun's changed citation year and the duplicated Li reference do not constitute new cited works.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative remain recognizable. Changes include targeted abstract and contribution rewrites, merging method subsections, replacing 'inter-model variance' with 'inter-client model deviation,' and reorganizing the experimental appendix. The extensive new scientific material does not itself establish extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column preprint layout to a two-column conference layout, with substantial figure relocation and resizing. v2 expands the baseline table and legends, redraws the topology comparison, and adds batching/subsampling charts, communication-volume plots, and a reconstruction-image panel.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful cost and privacy evidence, improves implementation documentation, narrows overclaims, and corrects Equation 4. However, its new central convergence theorem has a material problem: Theorem 4.5 permits eta=1/(8LT), which makes gamma in Equation 9a equal -7/(16L), undermining the stated upper bound. Hyperparameter selection also remains contradictory in Appendix C.2. These benefits and new reliability concerns prevent a confident net quality judgment.
